Title: New Application for Registering for an USI course

If you want to register for a course at the sports institute, you need to select a course.
If slots are free, the system tells you the courses, and dates.
Select one.
Next, you need to check if you already have an account at the sports institute.
If not, you need to check whether you are registered at an eligible university.
If you are, register your account.
If you are not, request an activation and wait for a response.
As soon as you have an account, log into it.
The application is also connected to your twitter account, and lets you tweet to friends who might want to join you, you can complete the registration for the course and provide the payment information.
In the end, you will receive a course ticket.

args.text: Name gateways as yes/no questions taken from the description condition, and name tasks with the action verb and object stated in the description

trace.reason: Check whether documented guidelines already cover labeling of gateways and tasks from description wording before proposing a label guideline.

result.rule: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.

args.text: Name an exclusive gateway as a yes/no question using the key words of the condition stated in the description, such as whether an account exists or whether slots are free

trace.reason: Check whether error-driven guidelines already cover gateway label wording before deciding on a relation.

result.rule: When the description states a yes/no condition that decides which branch follows a step, and the same condition is stated in the sentence that introduces that decision: Label the exclusive gateway as a yes/no question that repeats the condition in the description's own wording, and place it at the point where the description ties that condition to the step. Do not reuse a condition from a neighboring sentence or a condition about another action. Give the task that the condition controls the action verb and object the description uses, and do not add a separate reporting-style gateway or task that the description does not state.

When the description states a question that the customer is put to, where the customer's answer picks one of two or more options that are named in that question, and the steps that follow depend on the pick: Model the pick as an exclusive gateway placed where the description states it. Label the gateway with the named options in the description's own wording, phrased as the question the customer is asked. Label the preceding step that puts the question with the description's verb and object. Give each option its own labelled outgoing branch. Do not replace the gateway with a bare task, and do not paraphrase the options into different words.

When the description states a yes/no condition on the state of something and then gives the opposite case as its own separate sentence (for example 'If X, do A' followed by 'If not X, do B'), with the condition possibly followed by a further check on a different criterion: Model the condition as an exclusive gateway split with one labeled outgoing branch for each stated case, including the opposite case described in the separate sentence, and make the branch for the opposite case perform its stated action. If a further check on a different criterion follows one of the cases, place a second exclusive gateway on that branch. Rejoin alternative branches that reach a common later element with an exclusive merge placed just before it.

When the description states a check or question that is asked only when an earlier condition does not hold (for example, an 'if not' sentence that follows a positive 'if' sentence): Place that check after the earlier decision gateway, on the flow for the negative outcome, and do not place it before the gateway. Label the gateway with the condition the description states, and keep the check's label close to the description's wording for that branch.
